reviewedMapping.evidence: The parameterized helper executes every released canonical-resources step, including resource-specific representation negotiation, GeoJSON features and SensorML JSON items parsing, and all-page retrieval through bounded next links.

The parameterized helper executes media-type discovery, unsupported-media evidence, released endpoint retrieval, response-media-specific GeoJSON/SensorML collection parsing, HTTP validation, and all-page traversal.
The deployed TestNG method consumes canonicalResources for every supported Part 1 type, requires each local ID, and fails duplicate IDs within the same type; focused duplicate-ID coverage passes.

The deployed TestNG method consumes all supported canonical resources, gives normative SensorML uniqueId precedence followed by GeoJSON properties.uid and direct extension uid, validates absolute URI syntax, and rejects duplicate UIDs across resource types; focused conflicting-shape and cross-type duplication coverage passes.

The deployed TestNG method evaluates every retrieved UID, recognizes valid UUID URNs and namespaces in the bundled provenance-recorded IANA Formal and Informal URN Namespaces registry snapshot, and emits TestNG warnings rather than failures for other valid forms; focused recommendation-form and registry-integrity coverage passes.

The deployed TestNG method iterates advertised collections with temporal extents, queries released collection-items with instant, bounded, open-start, and open-end datetime forms, resolves now at captured request time, rejects non-intersecting validTime, requires unfiltered timeless IDs in every filtered result, and SKIPs with no eligible collection; focused positive, boundary, and fail-closed temporal coverage passes.

The deployed TestNG method evaluates every canonical System page, applies the released GeoJSON geometry and SensorML position mappings, exempts only Simulation and Process assets, and reports recommendation warnings without converting them to conformance failures.

The deployed TestNG method accepts the optional public mobile-system-id argument, dereferences that known moving System, applies representation-specific coordinate mappings, and requires a position change during bounded 30-second polling; SensorML orientation-only changes do not prove movement, and absent input produces an explicit SKIP rather than positive evidence.

The deployed TestNG method traverses every advertised sosa:System collection through the reviewed collection-items helper, requires one same-origin canonical URL per item, dereferences it with the source representation media type, and compares complete parsed content after removing only canonical links.

The deployed TestNG method retrieves its own canonical System evidence and invokes the endpoint-parameterized resources procedure for /systems. Every page is validated against the bundled released GeoJSON or SensorML System collection schema selected from the actual response media type; the complete pinned GeoJSON dependencies are provenance-bound by SHA-256, malformed wrappers/features/geometries fail closed, and unsupported media produces an explicit SKIP.

The independently executable deployed TestNG method retrieves its own evidence and executes the endpoint-parameterized released resources procedure against the fixed API-root /systems canonical endpoint through the reviewed canonical-resources traversal, including HTTP, media-type, pagination, collection-shape, and fail-closed schema evidence.

The independently executable deployed TestNG method selects every /collections entry with featureType=sosa:System, continues after unsupported collections, traverses every supported items page through the reviewed helper, invokes the same endpoint-parameterized schema procedure, and restricts each representation-specific System type to the five released SOSA URI or CURIE values. Direct HTTP regression coverage proves an earlier unsupported collection cannot hide a later invalid supported collection. It deliberately adds no collection-existence or itemType assertion absent from the released Annex A procedure.

The independently executable deployed TestNG method probes bounded, media-gated nested collections to select a parent with a nonempty subsystem collection without requiring local item ids, dereferences that parent System resource, counts exactly one rel=subsystems link occurrence, and requires its resolved URI to exactly equal the already-fetched api_root/systems/{id}/subsystems endpoint. It rejects duplicate-identical, trailing-slash, query, fragment, and cross-origin variants, reuses the accepted first response, establishes HTTP 200 and actual media before parsing every page, warns and SKIPs unsupported or absent media, and validates every supported page against the existing released GeoJSON or SensorML System collection schema.

The independently executable deployed TestNG method issues read-only /systems requests with the exact recursive=false and recursive=true query values and requires HTTP 200 for both without parsing representation content outside the released procedure. Controlled HTTP coverage records both exact query strings and proves successful non-JSON responses do not create unrelated failures.

The deployed TestNG method builds a bounded, iteratively cycle-rejecting hierarchy oracle solely from default direct-child subsystem endpoints, rejects shortcut overlap when a direct child is also reachable through a longer path, then proves default and recursive=false /systems exclude every discovered child while recursive=true includes all independently discovered hierarchy nodes. Blank and duplicate resource ids fail closed; absent hierarchy data produces an explicit SKIP.

The deployed TestNG method selects a parent with independently established transitive descendants, rejects direct-child shortcut overlap before evidence selection, proves default and recursive=false nested endpoints contain exactly direct children, and proves recursive=true contains every descendant. It never derives expected hierarchy membership from the recursive=true response itself.

For every independently discovered parent with subsystems, the deployed TestNG method probes canonical top-level samplingFeatures, datastreams, and controlstreams endpoints as independent implementation evidence. Once a type returns HTTP 200 there, every parent and descendant nested endpoint must return HTTP 200; all-parent 404 cannot become an unsupported-type SKIP. The method unions descendant resource ids and requires each parent endpoint to contain that closure. Top-level-unsupported types and an entirely empty descendant evidence set produce explicit SKIPs rather than positive conformance.
